title: Brooklyn Nets 2025-26 season predictions after NBA schedule release
content: The Brooklyn Nets are entering the 2025‑26 NBA season in a full‑scale rebuild after a 26‑56 finish last year, the second‑worst record in the league.  The team’s strategy centers on five rookie first‑round picks—Egor Demin, Nolan Traore, Drake Powell, Ben Saraf, and Danny Wolf—who are expected to make their debut in the same game, a first in NBA history.  Coach Jordi Fernandez will balance Demin’s playmaking role with the development of the other rookies, while the Nets aim to stay in the lottery rather than chase a playoff berth.  Projected performance places the Nets in the low‑20s for wins, with sportsbooks setting an over/under of about 20.5 wins, tied with the Washington Wizards for the second‑worst projection; only the Utah Jazz (18.5 projected wins) are expected to finish lower.  Key schedule storylines include a November 9 home loss to the New York Knicks (the Nets have lost 10 straight to them), four games against the Wizards that could influence lottery positioning, a January 4 return of Cam Johnson to the Nets, and matchups against the Nuggets and Utah that will test the young roster.  The Nets are projected to finish around 24‑58, likely 14th in the East, and will not qualify for the playoffs or the play‑in tournament.  The season’s focus is on player development and securing a top‑3 lottery pick for 2026, with hopes that Demin could contend for Rookie of the Year and that Porter Jr. might become a trade asset.  Overall, the 2025‑26 campaign is seen as the true start of the Nets’ long‑term rebuild.

title: Brooklyn Nets 2025-26 season preview: Best-case scenario? Finishing with the worst record in the NBA
content: The Brooklyn Nets' 2025-26 season preview highlights a team built around a youth-driven rebuild, entering the season as the youngest in the NBA with an average roster age of 23.6 years. Despite first-year head coach Jordi Fernández initially guiding the team to a .500 record and top-10 offensive efficiency, general manager Sean Marks traded veterans Dennis Schröder and Dorian Finney-Smith to reset the roster. The Nets secured the No. 8 pick in the 2025 NBA Draft, selecting Egor Dëmin from BYU, while also acquiring Drake Powell (22nd overall) and other young talent. However, both Dëmin and Powell face injury setbacks—Dëmin with a plantar fascia tear and Powell with left knee tendinopathy—delaying their availability. The team’s core includes young players like Cam Thomas, Ziaire Williams, Day'Ron Sharpe, and Noah Clowney, with limited NBA experience across the roster. The trade for MPJ (Michael Porter Jr.) was primarily a cap-space maneuver, converting future cash into an unprotected 2032 first-round pick from Denver. The Nets are projected to finish with the worst record in the NBA, ensuring a top-five pick in the 2026 Draft, with prospects like Darryn Peterson, A.J. Dybantsa, Cameron Boozer, and Nate Ament on the horizon. Fernández emphasizes player development over wins, with young players receiving significant minutes and opportunities. Despite some promising individual growth—such as Dëmin, Traoré, Saraf, or Bufkin showing potential—none have emerged as immediate difference-makers. The team’s focus remains on long-term rebuilding, with Marks open to trade discussions involving players like Terance Mann and Nic Claxton. The article concludes that while the Nets are winning more games than expected for a rebuild, their best-case scenario hinges on losing enough to secure a top-tier draft pick, underscoring the paradox of development through adversity.

title: What does the Nets' schedule look like throughout the 2025-26 season?
content: The Brooklyn Nets' schedule for the 2025-26 season has been released, with the toughest portion being the opening month of October. According to HoopsHype's Cyro Asseo, the Nets will face the Charlotte Hornets, Cleveland Cavaliers, San Antonio Spurs, Houston Rockets, and Atlanta Hawks in their first five games. Asseo used a Strength of Schedule (SOS) metric, which takes into account average over/under win projections from sportsbooks, to determine the Nets' schedule. The Cavaliers and Rockets were strong teams last season, but the Rockets have changed significantly with the trade for Kevin Durant. The Hawks, Spurs, and Hornets were teams with losing records, but the Hawks have improved with the trade for Kristaps Porzingis. Asseo noted, 'We used average over/under win projections from the most popular sportsbooks to build a month-by-month Strength of Schedule (SOS) for every NBA team in 2025-26.' The Nets are expected to be in the Lottery after next season, but October may be a tough beginning to what could be a long season.

title: Nets roll past Hapoel Jerusalem 123-88 in preseason opener
content: The Brooklyn Nets opened their preseason with a 123-88 victory over Hapoel Jerusalem at Barclays Center on October 5, 2025, under head coach Jordi Fernández, marking his second season with the team. The Nets dominated from the start, building a 34-22 lead in the first quarter and expanding it to 25 points by halftime. They showcased balanced scoring and aggressive full-court pressure, shooting 56.3% from the field and recording 31 assists on 49 made baskets while forcing 13 turnovers. Ben Saraf, the 26th overall pick in the 2025 draft, played 18 minutes, finishing with nine points and a team-high six assists despite picking up five fouls in his first 11 minutes, impressing with his handle, passing, and composure. Nolan Traoré, the 19th overall pick, scored seven points on 2-for-6 shooting, added two rebounds and two assists in 18 minutes, showing flashes of offensive creativity. Wolf, the 27th pick, entered in the second half and contributed five points, five rebounds, and five assists in 15 minutes, demonstrating versatility with his handle and passing. Terance Mann led all scorers with 15 points on 6-for-7 shooting, Michael Porter Jr. added 13 points, five rebounds, and four assists, and Nic Claxton recorded 11 points and eight rebounds. The Nets used a 10-man rotation in the first half, with 17 players seeing action overall. Egor Demin, Drake Powell, and Haywood Highsmith were sidelined due to injury. Coach Fernández confirmed that every healthy player is expected to play in the next two or three games. The Nets’ preseason continues in Macau, China, with two games against the Phoenix Suns. The performance of the rookies—Saraf, Traoré, and Wolf—highlighted both their potential and the growing pains the team anticipates navigating during the season.

title: Nets season preview: Is rebuilding Brooklyn team going anywhere? - CBSSports.com
content: At the 2023 trade deadline the Brooklyn Nets traded Kevin Durant and ended an era. They have since traded Mikal Bridges and Cam Johnson, amassing 32 draft picks over the next seven years, including a first‑rounder in 2026. General Manager Sean Marks said, 'Success for us looks like, how do we find, how do we determine who are the next Nets?' The Nets finished 26‑56 last season, giving them a 37.2 % chance of a top‑four pick. Coach Jordi Fernández earned praise after a 9‑10 start, but the team lost 21 of its final 26 games. The preview presents both a believer’s optimism—highlighting future picks such as Egor Dëmin and potential players like Darryn Peterson—and a skeptic’s caution about the rebuild’s timing and the 2027 pick swap. Overall, the article shows the Nets in rebuild mode, with the possibility of returning to win‑now play by 2026‑27.

title: 25 dias para a NBA: Brooklyn Nets aposta em nova safra de jovens para pavimentar futuro competitivo
content: The Brooklyn Nets finished the 2024‑25 season with a 26‑56 record, placing 12th in the Eastern Conference. Under rookie head coach Jordi Fernández, the team started with a roughly 50 % win rate until November, but injuries to Cam Thomas and the loss of Dennis Schroder and Dorian‑Finney Smith caused a decline. For 2025‑26 the Nets will field five first‑round draft picks: Egor Demin (8th), Nolan Traoré (19th), Drake Powell (22nd), Ben Saraf (26th) and Danny Wolf (27th). They added veteran guard Kobe Bufkin, wing Terance Mann, power‑forward Haywood Highsmith, forward‑center Michael Porter Jr. and center E.J. Liddell, while letting go of D’Angelo Russell, Keon Johnson, Maxwell Lewis, Tosan Evbuomwan, Cam Johnson and Trendon Watford. The projected starting five is Egor Demin, Terance Mann, Cam Thomas, Michael Porter Jr. and Nic Claxton. The Nets’ offseason trade for Porter Jr. and a 2032 first‑round pick underscores the franchise’s focus on youth and experimentation. General manager Sean Marks said, 'Nós nunca ouvimos o que as notícias dizem, não vemos as odds (de apostas) em Las Vegas. Só entramos para competir.' The article emphasizes patience, the need for player development, and the risk of a talent‑heavy roster lacking veteran leadership. Metrics cited include the 26‑56 record, 12th place finish, and the five first‑round picks. The piece presents facts and quotes without editorializing.

title: Nets Hope Michael Porter Jr. Regains Jordi Fernandez-Era Efficiency in Brooklyn
content: The Brooklyn Nets have reunited Michael Porter Jr. with his former coach Jordi Fernandez, who is now the team's lead man. Fernandez previously left the Denver Nuggets to become the Sacramento Kings' associate head coach. Porter has never been a multifaceted player, but he found more success under Fernandez's guidance, particularly in the 2020-21 season when he posted an elite-level 66.3% true shooting and 64.6% effective field goal percentage. Fernandez's return to Brooklyn is expected to bring out the best in Porter, who should become a more efficient scorer and better overall defender. With Porter's frame and the team's defensive-minded players, the Nets could emerge as one of the best defensive teams in the league. Fernandez has proven that the 'Brooklyn Grit' identity works, and with Porter as the offensive focal point, the team could sneak into the play-in in a weakened Eastern Conference.

title: Nets rookies Nolan Traore, Ben Saraf receive Jordi Fernandez challenge after ugly loss
content: In a preseason loss to the Phoenix Suns during the NBA China Games, Brooklyn Nets rookies Nolan Traore and Ben Saraf received a challenge from head coach Jordi Fernandez after struggling with ball-handling and decision-making. Traore recorded one assist and four turnovers in 17 minutes, while Saraf had zero assists and two turnovers in 19 minutes. The Nets committed 32 turnovers, leading to 42 points for the Suns. Fernandez acknowledged the pressure of NBA-level defense as a learning opportunity, stating, 'That's a good experience. Hopefully, moving forward, they can get better and handle that better, because [committing] 34 turnovers for 42 points is not good enough. You're not going to win many games in the NBA [that way].' Traore showed speed in transition and halfcourt, scoring six points on 3-of-5 shooting, while Saraf scored nine points on 2-of-5 shooting and 5-of-6 from the free-throw line, demonstrating physicality and craft. Both rookies were 0-for-3 from three-point range, as they were at Summer League. Danny Wolf, the 6-foot-11 rookie, was the most impressive, posting 11 points, five rebounds, and three assists in 14 minutes, though he also had three turnovers. Drake Powell, returning from a knee injury, made his NBA debut with six points, two rebounds, two assists, and a steal in 13 minutes, earning praise from Fernandez for his athleticism and two-way potential. Cam Thomas led the Nets with 22 points and six assists, while Michael Porter Jr. and Noah Clowney each scored 13, and Nic Claxton added 12 points, nine rebounds, and five assists. The Nets will face the Suns again on Sunday at 7 AM EST.
